text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Malawi Deputy High Court Registrar Quoto Bitiku said that the government's appeal case to the Supreme Court over acquital of former president Kamuzu Banda -- accused of ordering the killing of four senior politicians -- begins on February 2.
But Director of Public Prosecution Kamudoni Nyasulu cast doubts on the dates due to the "unsubstantive court record to warrant further grounds of appeal to commence."

- Efforts to curb rising road accidents hit problems after a man suspected to be supplying fake driving licences and road permits to unqualified drivers slipped out of police custody, Transport Minister Harry Thomson said.

- Deputy Police Chief Kennedy Chirambo failed to appear in court to answer charges of "contempt of court" when he ordered re-arrest of four Nigerians in November last year after they were granted bail by a Magistrate court.

- High Court Judge Eric Kumitsonyo said democracy and order in the country was slipping into a quandary because many Malawians were ignoring court orders, a practice which destroys the essence of democracy and justice.

- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party Treasurer General John Tembo said at political rally that he was impressed with press freedom in the country but warned of press gagging on the semi-official radio station, especially when news came from oposition parties.
